title: SDK orchestration: cross-runtime streaming + function-calls with schema-fork migration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Define and implement a stable, backward-compatible SDK surface that unifies streaming token/delta delivery, tool/function call orchestration, and structured JSON/avro-like outputs across TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs. This ticket covers: design, cross-language interfaces, one reference implementation per language, migration utilities (schema-fork compatibility helpers), tests, and a staged rollout plan.
goals: Provide a minimal core API (CallHandle + EventSnapshot) that supports: incremental stream frames, intermittent tool call invitations, partial structured output patches, and deterministic finalization signals.
Ship TypeScript/Python/Go examples and shims that map old streaming callbacks to the new event-framed surface with minimal user changes.
Include a migration helper library (schema-fork) that translates legacy streaming envelopes into the new EventSnapshot shape and validates schema changes at runtime.
Measure end-to-end latency and tokenization cost impact; keep perf regression <5% for typical LLM chat workloads.
Add telemetry hooks for per-call tools-invoked, schema-parse-errors, and streaming reconnects for monitoring in Console.
acceptance_criteria: TS/py/go SDKs expose CallHandle API and EventSnapshot frame type documented in README
Migration helper package installs and passes example conversion tests (legacyEnvelope -> EventSnapshot)
All language reference examples included in repo examples/stream-orch and linked in PRs
End-to-end integration tests for tool call roundtrip with streaming deltas (happy + network interruption + duplicate frames) pass in CI
No customer-facing breaking changes for existing non-streaming sync APIs; opt-in feature gate for new surface until GA
comments: 2026-03-11 - Sync: agreed to use EventSnapshot as the canonical wire frame. Decided to avoid adding a new transport header and instead embed minimal metadata in the JSON envelope for backwards compatibility. (Aisha)
2026-03-12 - Review: PM asked that telemetry include tool invocation counts and schema-parse-failures. Action: add telemetry hooks and Console dashboard (Marco)
2026-03-13 - Design feedback from runtime: prefer explicit 'finalized' boolean in frames instead of special event types to simplify kernel-level flush detection. Adjusted spec accordingly.
2026-03-14 - Blocker: Go SDK streaming grpc dependency has an API contract mismatch on half-close behavior. Eng infra investigating. (blocking subtask ENG-981235 created)
2026-03-14 - PR 1224 opened with TS surface; initial review requested from @sylvia and @chen. Demo scripts included for chat+tool orchestration.
example_snippets:
# Python reference: generator-style streaming with EventSnapshot
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY'))
call = client.start_call(model='redwood-2.2')

for frame in call.stream_events():  # yields EventSnapshot dicts
    if frame.get('type') == 'delta':
        print('delta chunk:', frame['payload'])
    elif frame.get('type') == 'tool-invoke':
        # call local tool and return result back to server
        res = run_local_tool(frame['payload'])
        call.send_tool_result(invocation_id=frame['id'], result=res)
    elif frame.get('finalized'):
        final = frame['payload']
        print('final JSON output:', final)

# migration helper example
from redwood.migration import legacy_to_event_snapshot
migrated = legacy_to_event_snapshot(raw_legacy_frame)
call.inject_frame(migrated)
